settings.definition_quote: There are $K$ arms indexed by $k =1, \cdots, K$, and the algorithm selects $N$ arms every round. ... We assume each arm $k$ has binary states, $\{0, 1\}$, which evolve as a Markov chain with transition matrix either $\atransition_{k}$ or $\ptransition_{k}$ ... We assume the system resets every episode of length $\eplen$, which is also known to the learner.

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: The Bayesian regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:tsrmab} satisfies the following bound \begin{equation*} BR(T) = \bigO (\sqrt{K\eplen^3 N^{3}T \log T}) = \bigO (\sqrt{mK\eplen^4 N^{3} \log (m\eplen)}). \end{equation*}

results.notes: Second form sqrt(n_ep*K*H^4*N^3*log(n_ep*H)) is identical since T=mL. Regret against value of deterministic policy mu(theta*). Horizon: algorithm does not take T as input (delta=1/T only in analysis). Setting is out of scope (restless/markovian).

symbols.N_sel: number of arms selected (active) per round (paper's N)

conditions: prior Q is discrete and puts non-zero mass q on theta*
competitor policy is the optimal policy
T is a multiple of L

source.label: thm:frequentist
source.quote: Suppose the prior $\prior$ is discrete and puts a non-zero mass on the parameter $\trueBandit$. Additionally, assume that the competitor policy is the optimal policy. Then Algorithm \ref{alg:tsrmab} satisfies the following bound \[ R(T;\trueBandit) = \bigO (\sqrt{K\eplen^3 N^{3}T \log T}) = \bigO (\sqrt{mK\eplen^4 N^{3} \log (m\eplen)}). \]

results.notes: Derived via q R(T;theta*) <= BR(T); the O hides a 1/q factor (instance-dependent). Regret defined via expected value functions, recorded as pseudo_regret.
